findings.title: Google credential saved as the zod safeParse result object instead of the key data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the key directly. Now `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` followed by `data: { key }` writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`. On the next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because access_token, refresh_token and the other fields are no longer at the top level. This happens in the default non-sync path, so every Google Calendar credential is corrupted the first time its token refreshes. The code should store `key.data`.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh returns a fetch Response but code reads `res.data`
findings.body: With credential sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. The code then reads `res?.data` and `token.access_token`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so this throws a TypeError. The surrounding catch swallows any error other than `invalid_grant` and returns the stale auth, so Google Calendar silently never refreshes in sync mode. The Response needs `.json()`, and its shape must be mapped to the gaxios `{ data }` form.

findings.title: Hubspot treats the sync endpoint's fetch Response as a HubspotToken and persists it
findings.body: When sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`, but the result is typed and used as `HubspotToken`. `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN. `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` is undefined. The `Response` object is then written to `credential.key` (`as any`), which serializes to roughly `{}` and wipes the stored Hubspot token. The body must be parsed and mapped to the token shape before use.

findings.title: Axios-style callers read `.data` from the fetch Response returned in sync mode
findings.body: Zoho CRM here, and Zoho Bigin in its CalendarService, call `refreshOAuthTokens` and then access `.data.error`, `.data.expires_in` and `.data.access_token`. Their normal path returns an axios response, but in sync mode the helper returns a `fetch` `Response`, so `.data` is undefined. This throws a TypeError (swallowed by the catch in Zoho CRM). Credential syncing therefore cannot work for these apps. The helper should return a normalized shape, or each caller must parse the body.

findings.title: Credential ID passed where the Cal.com user ID is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's row id as the third argument, which is `userId`. In sync mode this posts `calcomUserId=<credential id>` to the self-hoster's endpoint. The endpoint will return tokens for a different user, or none, so one user's tokens can be attached to another's credential. The refresh also runs for team credentials, which should have no user id. `credential.userId` has to be passed instead, and `biginAuth`/`refreshAccessToken` must carry it through.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, not 'any key'. The second silently overrides the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Zod strips unknown keys, so the parsed data contains only `access_token`. The expiry and every other field from the sync endpoint are dropped, contrary to the comment about numeric expiry. Callers then compute `expires_in * 1000` as NaN (Zoom) or never update the expiry (Office365). A real catch-all needs `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(...)`.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens
findings.body: If the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper sets the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers such as Office365 (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`; schema marks refresh_token optional) and Zoom (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) then persist this placeholder over the user's real refresh token. This applies in sync mode, where the minimal schema strips everything but access_token. It can also apply in normal mode when the provider omits a rotated token. Later refreshes without sync will fail permanently. The placeholder should not be merged into stored credentials.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: The new refresh logic calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `@calcom/prisma`. This fails type-check/build, and at runtime throws a ReferenceError inside `getClient`. That rejects `this.conn`, so every Salesforce operation fails.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation but builds the connection with the stale access token
findings.body: `getClient` (run in every constructor call) now POSTs a refresh request to Salesforce and stores the new token. The `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old key, so the connection uses the pre-refresh token rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. This also adds a network call and DB write on each service creation, regardless of expiry. It bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply to Salesforce. The check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable because HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText, and `response.ok` should be used.

findings.title: Sync endpoint is called unauthenticated, with no error handling or timeout
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no secret or auth header. Anyone who can reach it could request tokens for any `calcomUserId`, and Cal.com cannot prove who it is. The raw `Response` is returned without checking `response.ok`, so a 4xx/5xx body is passed to callers, which parse it as a token response. There is no timeout. At minimum the webhook secret or an auth header should be sent and non-OK responses rejected.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (not constant-time) and no HTTP method check
findings.body: The shared secret is compared with a plain `!==`, which is not timing-safe. A header sent as an array also fails to match. The handler accepts any HTTP method, not only POST. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and reject non-POST requests.

findings.title: Invalid body, bad ciphertext or bad JSON produce unhandled 500s
findings.body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError for malformed input, and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` throw on a wrong key or bad payload. None are caught, so authenticated callers get an opaque 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Use `safeParse` and wrap decryption and parsing in try/catch to return a clear 400. The decrypted `keys` are also stored without any validation of shape.

findings.title: find-then-create is racy and can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: `findFirst` followed by `update` or `create` is not atomic. Two concurrent webhooks for the same user and app both see no credential and both create one, yielding duplicates. Later reads use `findFirst`, so which credential gets refreshed or used is nondeterministic. Use a transaction or a unique constraint.

findings.title: Webex still validates the refresh response with the full schema, so sync mode always fails
findings.body: Zoom, Office365 and Salesforce route the refresh response through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but Webex still uses `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`. That schema requires scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented sync response contains only the access token and expiry, so with sync enabled the parse fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and Webex cannot refresh.

findings.title: No tests for the new sync flow
findings.body: The PR adds a credential-sync webhook, `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` across about ten providers without any tests, and the PR checklist says none were added. The bugs above (wrong stored key shape, bad schema keys, wrong user id, `.data` on a Response) would be caught by basic unit tests of the helpers and the webhook handler.
